chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-command detector only rejects exact option names in `_NARROWING`, so a pytest run that ignores the suite through a similarly named option is still treated as whole. chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper = avoidable / placed` is used to decide the falsifier and is described as an upper bound, but it is not a bound on the total avoidable share once `unplaced` runs exist. chunk_findings.detail: `test_unknown_trees_cannot_refute_the_falsifier` locks the falsifier to the wrong verdict on its own fixture. chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` treats any standalone `tests` or `tests/` token in a `unit_tests` command as proof that the whole suite ran, so commands that explicitly exclude the tests directory are misclassified as whole-suite runs. For example, given one real whole-suite run `pytest tests/` on a clean tree and a later `unit_tests` event on the same clean tree with command `pytest --ignore tests/`, `_is_suite` returns `True` for the second event, `classify` puts it in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`, and `build` reports an avoidable share of `1/2`. The second command does not run the whole `tests/` directory, so it should not be in `runs` at all; the correct report for that input has `runs=1`, `avoidable=0`, and `avoidable_share=0`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` returns a partial sum when some per-run values are missing, silently reporting an incomplete class total as if it were the figure. For example, a class containing one run with `elapsed_s=600` and one run with `elapsed_s` absent gets `suite_minutes=10.0` instead of `None` with an `unavailable` explanation. The module contract says a figure the log cannot give is `None` with a reason, but this input produces a non-`None` class minutes figure that cannot be trusted as the total.

chunk_findings.detail: A phase-scoped suitewaste query is classified against the whole log. The handler rejects an unknown phase, then calls `SW.build(events, cfg, now, probes, since=floor)` and never passes `phase`, while `swarm` on the same path does filter. Given events where phase `a` has only unavoidable whole-suite runs and phase `b` has avoidable ones, `metrics` view `suitewaste` with phase `a` still folds `b` into the avoidable share (and the reason breakdown), so the figure is not the phase the caller asked for.

chunk_findings.detail: `seen` stores only the first item that covered a code tree, so a later rework by another item is not classed as a same-item rerun. Given lane-b then lane-a then lane-a again on tree key K, the third run is `rerun_same_tree_other_item` because `seen[K]` is still lane-b. The module contract says a rerun is same-item when an earlier run of that tree was by the same item, so that input is `rerun_same_tree_same_item`.

chunk_findings.detail: Unplaced runs are unknown, but they still sit in the avoidable-share denominator and can refute the falsifier. With minimum 1, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and four `unplaced` rows give `avoidable_share` 0.2 and `falsifier.holds` false (`REFUTED`), even though those four name no tree git can read and the only placed run was avoidable. The claim “under 25 percent avoidable” is not shown; the unknowns are treated as non-avoidable.

chunk_findings.detail: The new phase filter excludes out-of-phase events from `SW.build` entirely, so they are also removed from the tree-history evidence used to decide whether an in-phase run is a rerun. Given `state` with `item-a` in phase `p` and `item-b` in phase `q`, and an event log containing (1) a whole-suite run by `item-b` on tree key `K`, then (2) a whole-suite run by `item-a` on the same tree key `K`, `metrics suitewaste --phase p` builds `scope` that returns false for `item-b`; the first run is never seen by the classifier, so the `item-a` run is reported as `first_run` with `avoidable_share` 0. The phase totals should omit the `item-b` run’s count/minutes, but the `item-a` run is still avoidable because an earlier run on the same code tree existed; this change reports it as unavoidable.

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-command detector only rejects exact option names in `_NARROWING`, so a pytest run that ignores the suite through a similarly named option is still treated as whole. For a `unit_tests` event whose command is `pytest --ignore-glob=tests/*.py tests/`, `shlex.split` yields `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py`; `t.split("=")[0]` is `--ignore-glob`, which is not in `_NARROWING`, and the token is skipped as an option. The remaining positional `tests/` matches `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns True and `_is_suite` counts the event as a whole-suite run, even though `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py` explicitly excludes the test files in `tests/`. This inflates whole-suite counts and can change the avoidable share.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper = avoidable / placed` is used to decide the falsifier and is described as an upper bound, but it is not a bound on the total avoidable share once `unplaced` runs exist. With `minimum=1`, one placed non-avoidable run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `avoidable=0`, `placed=1`, `upper=0.0`, and `falsifier.holds` false, so the output treats the “under 25 percent avoidable” condition as met even though those 99 unplaced runs could all be same-item reruns, making the true share 99/100. Conversely, one placed `rerun_same_tree_same_item` run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `upper=1.0` and `holds` true even though the true share could be 1/100 if the unplaced runs were first runs. Thus unknown trees can still drive the falsifier in either direction, contrary to the comment and the stated all-runs falsifier.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert not whole("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")` requires `_whole_command` to reject a command that includes the whole suite root `tests/`. Since the same test asserts `whole("pytest ./tests/")`, adding a file path inside that same root cannot make the command anything other than a whole-suite collection: `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/` still collects the entire `tests/` directory. If a `unit_tests` event uses that command as a rerun on a tree already run by the same item, this test locks in classifying the event as not a full-suite run, so the rerun is omitted from `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and the reported avoidable share is undercounted.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_unknown_trees_cannot_refute_the_falsifier` locks the falsifier to the wrong verdict on its own fixture. Unknowns must not force that refutation via the diluted 0.2, but the placed share is 0.5, which is not under 25 percent, so `holds` must be false (or unavailable), not true. chunk_findings.detail: The new `_falsifier` and the renamed `avoidable_share_max` still treat the passed `upper` as a true maximum avoidable share, but the value passed remains the old placed-only ratio rather than a bound over all runs once `unplaced` runs exist. Given a log with 1 placed whole-suite run that is not avoidable and 99 `unplaced` runs, `avoidable=0`, `share=0`, and `upper=0`; `_falsifier(0, 0)` returns `holds=False` and `verdict="refuted"`, and `text` prints `at most 0% if every unplaced run re-ran a tree`. But those 99 unknown-tree runs could all be avoidable reruns, making the maximum true avoidable share 99/100, so the under-25% falsifier cannot be refuted from this data. The upper bound must include the unplaced runs (for example, `(avoidable + unplaced) / runs`) or the falsifier must remain undetermined when unplaced runs exist.

chunk_findings.detail: The `suitewaste` branch accepts a `phase` argument (and the caller has already validated that it exists) but then silently drops it: `SW.build` is called only with `events`, `cfg`, `now`, `probes`, and `since=floor`, with no `phase` passed. Given a state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, and whole-suite runs only in `beta`, a call such as `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` returns the whole-suite classification and avoidable share for all events, including those from `beta`, as though they belonged to `alpha`. If `suitewaste` is intentionally global, the view should reject or explicitly ignore the phase parameter at the API/surface boundary; silently accepting and discarding it makes phase-scoped metrics wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: The whole-suite test detection is based only on a standalone `tests`/`tests/` token, so it both over- and under-classifies `unit_tests` runs. For example, a `unit_tests` event with evidence command `pytest tests -k test_one` (or `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_slow.py`) matches `_WHOLE` because it sees `tests` followed by whitespace, so `_is_suite` returns True and the run is counted/classified as a whole-suite run even though it runs only a subset. Conversely, `pytest ./tests` is a whole-directory run but does not match because `tests` is preceded by `/`, not start/whitespace, so that run is omitted. Either input changes `runs`, class counts, and `avoidable_share`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` silently sums only the known values, so class and avoidable minute totals can be incomplete but still reported as complete figures. For example, if a class has two runs, one with `elapsed_s=60` and one with missing/invalid `elapsed_s` (so `suite_s=None`), `classes[c]["suite_minutes"]` becomes `1.0`, not `None`, even though the class total suite minutes are unknown and could be much larger. The same applies to `avoidable_suite_minutes` when some avoidable reruns lack `elapsed_s`. This contradicts the module’s contract that a figure the log cannot give is `None` with an unavailable reason, not a partial/zero-looking total.

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` returns false unless `evidence.command` is a non-empty string, before the `gate == "ci"` check. A `gate.passed` (or failed) event with `gate=ci`, `tree_sha` `abcdef1+clean`, and `elapsed_s` set but command omitted is dropped by `runs`, so it never receives a class and is missing from `avoidable_share`. The module’s own definition counts every `ci` verdict as a whole-suite run; the command test only belongs on `unit_tests`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_WHOLE` only matches a `tests` token bounded by whitespace or the ends of the string, so a real whole-directory `unit_tests` command is not a suite run. Given `command="pytest ./tests/"`, `gate=unit_tests`, a clean sha, and `kind=passed`, `_WHOLE.search` fails (`/` precedes `tests`), `runs` omits the event, and both the class counts and the avoidable share are computed on the wrong set. The same pattern false-positives `pytest tests/test_foo.py --basetemp tests` because the trailing `tests` token matches even though the suite directory was not run.

chunk_findings.detail: `avoidable_share` is `avoidable / n` where `n` includes `unplaced` runs, which are defined as not avoidable and not classifiable. chunk_findings.detail: `build` now filters by `in_scope` before calling `classify`, so out-of-scope runs no longer contribute to the tree history used to decide whether an in-scope run is a rerun. If a passed run for item `beta` on clean tree `abcdef1+clean` is followed by a passed run for item `alpha` on the same tree, calling with `in_scope=lambda item: item == "alpha"` gives the `alpha` row class `first_on_tree` and avoidable share `0`, because the classifier never sees the earlier `beta` run. That is wrong for the stated metric: the `alpha` run is a rerun on a tree whose code paths already ran, so it should be classified as `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and counted as avoidable while still leaving `beta` out of the reported totals.

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed partial-minute defect still stands: `_minutes` returns `round(sum(known) / 60.0, 2)` whenever at least one value is known. chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed falsifier denominator defect also remains: `avoidable_share` is still computed over all scoped rows, including `unplaced` rows that are defined as not classifiable. The new `in_scope` filtering does not change this for the default no-phase call, so unknown trees continue to count as evidence against the cache-first conclusion.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper` value is used as the falsifier’s decisive share and is described as an upper bound, but `avoidable / placed` is not an upper bound on the overall avoidable share. The unplaced runs are unknown and could be avoidable; excluding them from the denominator can make the reported share too low. For example, with `minimum=1`, suppose there are 10 whole-suite runs: 9 are placed, of which 2 are avoidable and 7 are not, and 1 is unplaced. Then `placed=9`, `avoidable=2`, `upper=2/9≈22%`, so `falsifier.holds` is false and `text` reports the cache-first order as refuted. If that one unplaced run is actually a same-tree rerun, the avoidable share is `3/10=30%`, above the 25% threshold, so the data do not establish a refutation. The comment’s premise is false: the correct upper bound accounting for unknown trees would include the unplaced runs in the numerator, not simply drop them from the denominator.

chunk_findings.detail: The new falsifier and output treat `upper` as a true upper bound on the overall avoidable share (`avoidable_share_max`, “at most … if every unplaced run re-ran a tree”), but the value passed in is still the old `avoidable_share_of_placed` value (`avoidable / placed`); this diff renames the key and changes the verdict logic but does not recompute `upper` as the maximum possible share. For example, with 5 placed whole-suite runs of which 1 is avoidable and 1 unplaced run, `upper = 1/5 = 0.20` and `share = 1/6`, so `_falsifier` returns `holds=False` and the text reports “refuted” and “at most 20% …”. If that unplaced run is avoidable, the true overall avoidable share is `2/6 = 33%`, so the report falsely refutes the cache-first order and understates the possible share. This is the previously confirmed upper-bound defect still present in the new `_falsifier`/max-key path.

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test is still only a direct unit test of an `in_scope` callback; it never passes a phase to the metrics service or exercises the `--phase` path that was previously reported as dropped. It calls `_report(ev, ..., in_scope=lambda i: i == "A")`, so it proves that a supplied item predicate keeps tree history, but it does not prove that a phase name such as `alpha` is converted into that predicate. If the service path for `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` still ignores the phase and classifies all items, a state with whole-suite runs only in phase `beta` would still be reported for `--phase alpha`, and this test would remain green.

chunk_findings.detail: The updated test still does not place a timed run and an untimed run in the same class. `rerun_same_tree_same_item` contains only a timed run, and `rerun_same_tree_other_item` contains only an untimed run. The previously confirmed partial-minute failure mode is a class with one known `elapsed_s` and one missing/invalid `elapsed_s`; that class is never constructed here. If `_minutes` returns the sum of known elapsed values whenever any value is known, a class with one 600-second run and one untimed run would report `suite_minutes == 10.0` and still count the untimed run, but this test would pass because no class has that mixed timed/untimed membership.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The falsifier verdict function `_falsifier` returns `undetermined` when the lower bound reaches or exceeds the threshold (`lower >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, which yields `holds = True` then `verdict = "stands"`), but if `lower < FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, `lower` is not `>= FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper` is not `< FALSIFIER_SHARE`, so `holds` evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. However, if `lower` is `None` or `upper` is `None`, `holds` also evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. Given a dataset where `lower = 0.2` and `upper = 0.3` (`FALSIFIER_SHARE = 0.25`), `lower < 0.25` and `upper >= 0.25`, so `holds` becomes `None` (undetermined). But the research principle R-suite-lock-principles-2026-11-12 defines refutation specifically when *even the upper bound* is under the threshold (`upper < FALSIFIER_SHARE`), meaning an upper bound of 30% cannot be refuted; however, a lower bound below 25% with an upper bound at or above 25% does not mean the cache-first order stands either, yet returning `"undetermined"` conflates missing data (`None`) with an inconclusive bound where the upper bound exceeds the threshold.

chunk_findings.detail: The option-value half of the whole-suite detector is still wrong after the rewrite. `return any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` treats every token as a collected path, so a directory that is only an option value still forces a suite match. chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed unplaced-share defect is not fixed. `share = avoidable / n` still divides by every scoped row, including `unplaced`. chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` treats any standalone `tests` or `tests/` token in a `unit_tests` command as proof that the whole suite ran, so commands that explicitly exclude the tests directory are misclassified as whole-suite runs. For example, given one real whole-suite run `pytest tests/` on a clean tree and a later `unit_tests` event on the same clean tree with command `pytest --ignore tests/`, `_is_suite` returns `True` for the second event, `classify` puts it in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`, and `build` reports an avoidable share of `1/2`. The second command does not run the whole `tests/` directory, so it should not be in `runs` at all; the correct report for that input has `runs=1`, `avoidable=0`, and `avoidable_share=0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_is_suite

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` returns a partial sum when some per-run values are missing, silently reporting an incomplete class total as if it were the figure. For example, a class containing one run with `elapsed_s=600` and one run with `elapsed_s` absent gets `suite_minutes=10.0` instead of `None` with an `unavailable` explanation. The module contract says a figure the log cannot give is `None` with a reason, but this input produces a non-`None` class minutes figure that cannot be trusted as the total.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: A phase-scoped suitewaste query is classified against the whole log. The handler rejects an unknown phase, then calls `SW.build(events, cfg, now, probes, since=floor)` and never passes `phase`, while `swarm` on the same path does filter. Given events where phase `a` has only unavoidable whole-suite runs and phase `b` has avoidable ones, `metrics` view `suitewaste` with phase `a` still folds `b` into the avoidable share (and the reason breakdown), so the figure is not the phase the caller asked for.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:_own_fold

chunk_findings.detail: `seen` stores only the first item that covered a code tree, so a later rework by another item is not classed as a same-item rerun. Given lane-b then lane-a then lane-a again on tree key K, the third run is `rerun_same_tree_other_item` because `seen[K]` is still lane-b. The module contract says a rerun is same-item when an earlier run of that tree was by the same item, so that input is `rerun_same_tree_same_item`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:131

chunk_findings.detail: Unplaced runs are unknown, but they still sit in the avoidable-share denominator and can refute the falsifier. With minimum 1, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and four `unplaced` rows give `avoidable_share` 0.2 and `falsifier.holds` false (`REFUTED`), even though those four name no tree git can read and the only placed run was avoidable. The claim “under 25 percent avoidable” is not shown; the unknowns are treated as non-avoidable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:191

chunk_findings.detail: The new phase filter excludes out-of-phase events from `SW.build` entirely, so they are also removed from the tree-history evidence used to decide whether an in-phase run is a rerun. Given `state` with `item-a` in phase `p` and `item-b` in phase `q`, and an event log containing (1) a whole-suite run by `item-b` on tree key `K`, then (2) a whole-suite run by `item-a` on the same tree key `K`, `metrics suitewaste --phase p` builds `scope` that returns false for `item-b`; the first run is never seen by the classifier, so the `item-a` run is reported as `first_run` with `avoidable_share` 0. The phase totals should omit the `item-b` run’s count/minutes, but the `item-a` run is still avoidable because an earlier run on the same code tree existed; this change reports it as unavoidable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:129 (`scope` / `_own_fold`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-command detector only rejects exact option names in `_NARROWING`, so a pytest run that ignores the suite through a similarly named option is still treated as whole. For a `unit_tests` event whose command is `pytest --ignore-glob=tests/*.py tests/`, `shlex.split` yields `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py`; `t.split("=")[0]` is `--ignore-glob`, which is not in `_NARROWING`, and the token is skipped as an option. The remaining positional `tests/` matches `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns True and `_is_suite` counts the event as a whole-suite run, even though `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py` explicitly excludes the test files in `tests/`. This inflates whole-suite counts and can change the avoidable share.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper = avoidable / placed` is used to decide the falsifier and is described as an upper bound, but it is not a bound on the total avoidable share once `unplaced` runs exist. With `minimum=1`, one placed non-avoidable run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `avoidable=0`, `placed=1`, `upper=0.0`, and `falsifier.holds` false, so the output treats the “under 25 percent avoidable” condition as met even though those 99 unplaced runs could all be same-item reruns, making the true share 99/100. Conversely, one placed `rerun_same_tree_same_item` run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `upper=1.0` and `holds` true even though the true share could be 1/100 if the unplaced runs were first runs. Thus unknown trees can still drive the falsifier in either direction, contrary to the comment and the stated all-runs falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:avoidable_share_of_placed

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert not whole("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")` requires `_whole_command` to reject a command that includes the whole suite root `tests/`. Since the same test asserts `whole("pytest ./tests/")`, adding a file path inside that same root cannot make the command anything other than a whole-suite collection: `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/` still collects the entire `tests/` directory. If a `unit_tests` event uses that command as a rerun on a tree already run by the same item, this test locks in classifying the event as not a full-suite run, so the rerun is omitted from `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and the reported avoidable share is undercounted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:192

chunk_findings.detail: `_NARROWING` treats `--ff` as suite-narrowing, but pytest `--ff` / `--failed-first` still runs every test and only reorders failures first. Given a recorded whole-suite command `pytest --ff tests/` (or `pytest tests/ --ff`) after a real `pytest tests/` on the same clean tree, `_whole_command` returns False, the rerun is dropped from `runs`, and `build` under-counts avoidable suite minutes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The parser never consumes option arguments and does not treat `--ignore-glob` as narrowing, so it both misses real whole-suite runs and still accepts narrowed ones. `pytest --junitxml tests/out.xml tests/` (or `pytest --basetemp tests/tmp tests/`) has a non-option token `tests/out.xml` / `tests/tmp` that fails `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns False even though the selected path is the whole `tests/` tree. The inverse, `pytest tests/ --ignore-glob='test_*.py'`, has no token in `_NARROWING` and a root `tests/` path, so it returns True and is classed as a whole-suite rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: `test_unknown_trees_cannot_refute_the_falsifier` locks the falsifier to the wrong verdict on its own fixture. Two placed runs on tree `T` (first plus one same-item rerun) and three unplaced runs give `avoidable_share` 0.2 and `avoidable_share_of_placed` 0.5, and the test requires `falsifier.holds is True`. The prior contract treats `holds` false as the “under 25 percent avoidable” claim being refuted. Unknowns must not force that refutation via the diluted 0.2, but the placed share is 0.5, which is not under 25 percent, so `holds` must be false (or unavailable), not true. An implementation that follows this assertion reports the falsifier as holding when half of the runs git can place were avoidable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:182

A classifier that only special-cases `--ignore=` (or only an ignore of a subdirectory) still returns true for `--ignore tests/`, so that second event is still counted as a whole-suite rerun and the probe stays green.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_falsifier` and the renamed `avoidable_share_max` still treat the passed `upper` as a true maximum avoidable share, but the value passed remains the old placed-only ratio rather than a bound over all runs once `unplaced` runs exist. Given a log with 1 placed whole-suite run that is not avoidable and 99 `unplaced` runs, `avoidable=0`, `share=0`, and `upper=0`; `_falsifier(0, 0)` returns `holds=False` and `verdict="refuted"`, and `text` prints `at most 0% if every unplaced run re-ran a tree`. But those 99 unknown-tree runs could all be avoidable reruns, making the maximum true avoidable share 99/100, so the under-25% falsifier cannot be refuted from this data. The upper bound must include the unplaced runs (for example, `(avoidable + unplaced) / runs`) or the falsifier must remain undetermined when unplaced runs exist.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten probe still never creates a class containing both a timed and an untimed run. The fixture puts A's timed rerun alone in `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and B's untimed rerun alone in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`. Therefore an implementation of `_minutes` that sums only present `elapsed_s` values (`[600, None] -> 10.0`) passes the assertions, even though the class would have `untimed == 1` and incomplete minutes. The previous confirmed partial-sum defect remains untested; a mixed class (for example, A first timed, A second timed, and A third with only `tree_sha` on the same tree) is needed to demonstrate it.

chunk_findings.detail: Prefix `startswith` treats non-narrowing pytest options as suite-narrowing. `_NARROWING` contains `--lf`, and `--lfnf=all`.startswith(`--lf`) is true, so `_whole_command("pytest --lfnf=all tests/")` returns False even though `--lfnf` only sets last-failed-no-failures behavior and the selected path is the whole `tests/` tree. A later `unit_tests` event with that command on a tree already covered by `pytest tests/` is dropped from `runs`, so avoidable suite-minutes are under-counted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement `any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` still does not consume option arguments, so a directory that is only an option value counts as the suite root. For `pytest --basetemp tests/ tests/test_a.py`, `shlex` yields args `--basetemp`, `tests/`, `tests/test_a.py`; nothing matches a `_NARROWING` prefix, `_ROOT` matches the `--basetemp` value `tests/`, and `_whole_command` returns True. Pytest collects only `tests/test_a.py`. The same false whole-suite classification hits `pytest --rootdir tests/ tests/unit/test_a.py`. A same-item rerun recorded with that command is then counted as avoidable whole-suite waste.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:93

chunk_findings.detail: `test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes` still never puts a timed run and an untimed run in the same class, so it does not lock the partial-sum bug the probe was supposed to catch. `_log` records item A twice on tree `T` with `_ev` (elapsed present) and item B once on `T` with only `tree_sha`. That yields `rerun_same_tree_same_item` = (1, 10.0, 0) and `rerun_same_tree_other_item` = (1, None, 1). Both assertions pass if `_minutes` drops missing elapsed and returns the sum of the timed samples alone: a same-item class of `elapsed_s=600` plus one run with no elapsed would still report `suite_minutes == 10.0` and `untimed == 1`, and this test would not fail.
