chunk_findings.detail: The new short-option check only inspects the first two characters of an argument, so a combined short option whose last flag is `-k` or `-m` is not treated as narrowing. For the common invocation `pytest -vk tests/` (equivalent to `-v -k tests/`), `_narrows('-vk')` returns False because `arg[:2]` is `-v`; `_positionals` then treats the following `tests/` as a positional path, `_ROOT.match` matches it, and `_whole_command` returns True. The run is keyword-narrowed, not a whole-suite run, so it can be classified as whole and later runs on the same tree can be counted as avoidable reruns. The same failure occurs for combined marker options such as `pytest -vm marker tests/`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: Switching narrowing from a prefix test to an exact option name drops the companion flags the old `--sw` / `--stepwise` prefixes used to reject. Given `pytest --sw-skip tests/` or `pytest --stepwise-skip tests/`, `_narrows` is false for every arg and `_positionals` still sees `tests/`, so `_whole_command` returns True. Pytest still stops at the next failure after skipping the first, the same early exit `--stepwise` is listed to exclude, so that run is counted as a full-suite run and its suite-minutes land in the waste totals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: The `suitewaste` branch accepts a `phase` argument (and the caller has already validated that it exists) but then silently drops it: `SW.build` is called only with `events`, `cfg`, `now`, `probes`, and `since=floor`, with no `phase` passed. Given a state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, and whole-suite runs only in `beta`, a call such as `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` returns the whole-suite classification and avoidable share for all events, including those from `beta`, as though they belonged to `alpha`. If `suitewaste` is intentionally global, the view should reject or explicitly ignore the phase parameter at the API/surface boundary; silently accepting and discarding it makes phase-scoped metrics wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:_own_fold

chunk_findings.detail: The whole-suite test detection is based only on a standalone `tests`/`tests/` token, so it both over- and under-classifies `unit_tests` runs. For example, a `unit_tests` event with evidence command `pytest tests -k test_one` (or `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_slow.py`) matches `_WHOLE` because it sees `tests` followed by whitespace, so `_is_suite` returns True and the run is counted/classified as a whole-suite run even though it runs only a subset. Conversely, `pytest ./tests` is a whole-directory run but does not match because `tests` is preceded by `/`, not start/whitespace, so that run is omitted. Either input changes `runs`, class counts, and `avoidable_share`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_WHOLE

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` silently sums only the known values, so class and avoidable minute totals can be incomplete but still reported as complete figures. For example, if a class has two runs, one with `elapsed_s=60` and one with missing/invalid `elapsed_s` (so `suite_s=None`), `classes[c]["suite_minutes"]` becomes `1.0`, not `None`, even though the class total suite minutes are unknown and could be much larger. The same applies to `avoidable_suite_minutes` when some avoidable reruns lack `elapsed_s`. This contradicts the module’s contract that a figure the log cannot give is `None` with an unavailable reason, not a partial/zero-looking total.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` returns false unless `evidence.command` is a non-empty string, before the `gate == "ci"` check. A `gate.passed` (or failed) event with `gate=ci`, `tree_sha` `abcdef1+clean`, and `elapsed_s` set but command omitted is dropped by `runs`, so it never receives a class and is missing from `avoidable_share`. The module’s own definition counts every `ci` verdict as a whole-suite run; the command test only belongs on `unit_tests`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:79

chunk_findings.detail: `_WHOLE` only matches a `tests` token bounded by whitespace or the ends of the string, so a real whole-directory `unit_tests` command is not a suite run. Given `command="pytest ./tests/"`, `gate=unit_tests`, a clean sha, and `kind=passed`, `_WHOLE.search` fails (`/` precedes `tests`), `runs` omits the event, and both the class counts and the avoidable share are computed on the wrong set. The same pattern false-positives `pytest tests/test_foo.py --basetemp tests` because the trailing `tests` token matches even though the suite directory was not run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `avoidable_share` is `avoidable / n` where `n` includes `unplaced` runs, which are defined as not avoidable and not classifiable. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, share is 0.1, `falsifier.holds` is false, and `text` prints `REFUTED`, even though the only run git could place was avoidable (share 1.0 if unplaced were left out of the denominator). Unknown trees therefore count as evidence against the cache and can trip the 25% falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:175

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-suite detector still misclassifies ordinary pytest invocations because it scans the entire command line for “narrowing” tokens instead of only pytest arguments. Given `command="python -m pytest tests"`, `shlex.split` produces `['python', '-m', 'pytest', 'tests']`; the `any(...)` check sees `-m` and returns `False`, so `_is_suite` drops a real whole-suite run even though `-m` here is the Python module option, not pytest marker selection. Conversely, `command="pytest tests --ignore-glob=tests/test_slow.py"` is accepted as a whole-suite run because `--ignore-glob` is not in `_NARROWING`, even though that option deliberately excludes a test file from the run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: `build` now filters by `in_scope` before calling `classify`, so out-of-scope runs no longer contribute to the tree history used to decide whether an in-scope run is a rerun. If a passed run for item `beta` on clean tree `abcdef1+clean` is followed by a passed run for item `alpha` on the same tree, calling with `in_scope=lambda item: item == "alpha"` gives the `alpha` row class `first_on_tree` and avoidable share `0`, because the classifier never sees the earlier `beta` run. That is wrong for the stated metric: the `alpha` run is a rerun on a tree whose code paths already ran, so it should be classified as `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and counted as avoidable while still leaving `beta` out of the reported totals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed partial-minute defect still stands: `_minutes` returns `round(sum(known) / 60.0, 2)` whenever at least one value is known. For a class containing one run with `elapsed_s=60` and one run whose `elapsed_s` is missing or invalid, the class `suite_minutes` becomes `1.0`, not `None`, so a partial sum is still reported as if it were the complete class total. The diff adds a docstring saying an `untimed` count is reported beside the minutes, but the changed build path does not add that count to the class totals, so the reported minutes can still be incomplete while appearing complete.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed falsifier denominator defect also remains: `avoidable_share` is still computed over all scoped rows, including `unplaced` rows that are defined as not classifiable. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, the share is `0.1`, `falsifier.holds` is false, and the output reports `REFUTED`, even though every run that git could place was avoidable (share `1.0` if unknown trees were excluded). The new `in_scope` filtering does not change this for the default no-phase call, so unknown trees continue to count as evidence against the cache-first conclusion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper` value is used as the falsifier’s decisive share and is described as an upper bound, but `avoidable / placed` is not an upper bound on the overall avoidable share. The unplaced runs are unknown and could be avoidable; excluding them from the denominator can make the reported share too low. For example, with `minimum=1`, suppose there are 10 whole-suite runs: 9 are placed, of which 2 are avoidable and 7 are not, and 1 is unplaced. Then `placed=9`, `avoidable=2`, `upper=2/9≈22%`, so `falsifier.holds` is false and `text` reports the cache-first order as refuted. If that one unplaced run is actually a same-tree rerun, the avoidable share is `3/10=30%`, above the 25% threshold, so the data do not establish a refutation. The comment’s premise is false: the correct upper bound accounting for unknown trees would include the unplaced runs in the numerator, not simply drop them from the denominator.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:upper

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `not whole("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")`, but that command is a whole-suite run: pytest treats `tests/` as a directory argument and collects the entire suite, while the extra `tests/test_a.py` argument only adds a duplicate/redundant selection. If `_whole_command` follows this assertion, a `unit_tests` event with command `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/` will not be counted as a whole-suite run. For example, if that is the second run on the same code tree, it should be classified as an avoidable rerun, but it is omitted from `runs` and `avoidable_share`, understating the avoidable share.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_whole_suite_command_detection

chunk_findings.detail: Option values are treated as test paths. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest tests --basetemp tests/tmp"`, `kind=passed`, and a clean sha, `tests/tmp` matches `^(\./)?tests` but not `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns False and `runs` drops a whole-directory run. The inverse is `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`: the only token matching that prefix is the basetemp directory `tests`, `_ROOT` matches it, and a single-file run is counted as a whole-suite run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: Narrowing flags are only matched as exact tokens in `_NARROWING`. Given `command="pytest tests -ktest_one"` (argparse accepts the attached short option), `-ktest_one` is not in `_NARROWING`, the only collected path is `tests`, and `_is_suite` returns True for a selected subset. `command="pytest tests --ignore-glob=test_slow.py"` has the same result: `--ignore-glob` is never consulted, so an ignored subset is classified and counted as a whole-suite run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The probe that was supposed to lock the dropped `phase` argument never calls the metrics service and never passes a phase name. It only hands `_report` an `in_scope` callback over two items. A state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, whole-suite runs only in `beta`, and `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` can still classify the `beta` events, and this test stays green. The confirmed service-path drop is therefore not answered by the new test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_leaves_other_items_out

chunk_findings.detail: The untimed-minutes probe never puts a timed run and an untimed run in the same class. Item A is a timed first run on tree T; item B is the only member of `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and has no `elapsed_s`. Summing only the known values over an empty set already yields `None`, so the test passes on the unfixed `_minutes`. Given one class with `elapsed_s=60` and a second run whose `elapsed_s` is missing, the old code still reports `suite_minutes` of `1.0` instead of unknown.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_not_summed_as_zero

chunk_findings.detail: `_whole_command` still treats pytest option values as collection paths. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`, `shlex.split` yields args after `pytest` of `["test_foo.py", "--basetemp", "tests"]`; the changed line `return any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` returns `True` because the `--basetemp` value is `tests`, even though pytest collects only `test_foo.py`. If this single-file run occurs twice on the same code tree, the second run is counted as a whole-suite rerun and inflates the avoidable share, while a command such as `pytest tests --basetemp -m` can be incorrectly rejected because an option value starts with `-m`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The new falsifier and output treat `upper` as a true upper bound on the overall avoidable share (`avoidable_share_max`, “at most … if every unplaced run re-ran a tree”), but the value passed in is still the old `avoidable_share_of_placed` value (`avoidable / placed`); this diff renames the key and changes the verdict logic but does not recompute `upper` as the maximum possible share. For example, with 5 placed whole-suite runs of which 1 is avoidable and 1 unplaced run, `upper = 1/5 = 0.20` and `share = 1/6`, so `_falsifier` returns `holds=False` and the text reports “refuted” and “at most 20% …”. If that unplaced run is avoidable, the true overall avoidable share is `2/6 = 33%`, so the report falsely refutes the cache-first order and understates the possible share. This is the previously confirmed upper-bound defect still present in the new `_falsifier`/max-key path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_falsifier / `avoidable_share_max`

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test is still only a direct unit test of an `in_scope` callback; it never passes a phase to the metrics service or exercises the `--phase` path that was previously reported as dropped. It calls `_report(ev, ..., in_scope=lambda i: i == "A")`, so it proves that a supplied item predicate keeps tree history, but it does not prove that a phase name such as `alpha` is converted into that predicate. If the service path for `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` still ignores the phase and classifies all items, a state with whole-suite runs only in phase `beta` would still be reported for `--phase alpha`, and this test would remain green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_reports_only_its_items_but_keeps_the_tree_history

chunk_findings.detail: The updated test still does not place a timed run and an untimed run in the same class. `rerun_same_tree_same_item` contains only a timed run, and `rerun_same_tree_other_item` contains only an untimed run. The previously confirmed partial-minute failure mode is a class with one known `elapsed_s` and one missing/invalid `elapsed_s`; that class is never constructed here. If `_minutes` returns the sum of known elapsed values whenever any value is known, a class with one 600-second run and one untimed run would report `suite_minutes == 10.0` and still count the untimed run, but this test would pass because no class has that mixed timed/untimed membership.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The falsifier verdict function `_falsifier` returns `undetermined` when the lower bound reaches or exceeds the threshold (`lower >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, which yields `holds = True` then `verdict = "stands"`), but if `lower < FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, `lower` is not `>= FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper` is not `< FALSIFIER_SHARE`, so `holds` evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. However, if `lower` is `None` or `upper` is `None`, `holds` also evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. Given a dataset where `lower = 0.2` and `upper = 0.3` (`FALSIFIER_SHARE = 0.25`), `lower < 0.25` and `upper >= 0.25`, so `holds` becomes `None` (undetermined). But the research principle R-suite-lock-principles-2026-11-12 defines refutation specifically when *even the upper bound* is under the threshold (`upper < FALSIFIER_SHARE`), meaning an upper bound of 30% cannot be refuted; however, a lower bound below 25% with an upper bound at or above 25% does not mean the cache-first order stands either, yet returning `"undetermined"` conflates missing data (`None`) with an inconclusive bound where the upper bound exceeds the threshold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:236

chunk_findings.detail: The option-value half of the whole-suite detector is still wrong after the rewrite. `return any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` treats every token as a collected path, so a directory that is only an option value still forces a suite match. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`, `kind=passed`, and a clean sha, `tests` matches `_ROOT` and `_whole_command` returns True, so a single-file run is counted as a whole-suite run and can be classed `rerun_same_tree_*` (and added to the avoidable share) when it is the second event on that tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed unplaced-share defect is not fixed. `share = avoidable / n` still divides by every scoped row, including `unplaced`. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, `avoidable_share` is `0.1`, not `1.0`. Those nine rows are defined as not classifiable; leaving them in the denominator still reports a placed-avoidable share of 100% as 10%, which is the figure `has_figures` and the “avoidable N (X%)” line publish. The new upper bound only changes the falsifier verdict to `undetermined`; it does not take unplaced runs out of the share.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed probe still does not put a timed run and an untimed run in the same class, so it passes the unfixed `_minutes`. A is a timed pair on tree T (`rerun_same_tree_same_item`: one timed rerun, `suite_minutes` 10.0, `untimed` 0). B is the only member of `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and has no `elapsed_s`, so `suite_minutes is None` is just the empty known-set case. A class with `elapsed_s=60` plus a second run whose `elapsed_s` is missing still reports `1.0` instead of unknown, and this test stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The probe still asserts the denominator bug it is named to forbid. The unchanged setup is one placed avoidable rerun plus unplaced runs (1 of 5 overall, 1 of 2 placed), and the edited test still requires `avoidable_share == 0.2` while only adding `avoidable_share_max == 0.8` and `verdict == "undetermined"`. Unfixed code that divides by every scoped row, including `unplaced`, still returns 0.2 and passes. The share that excludes unknown trees is 0.5, which this test never demands.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_unplaced_runs_do_not_count_in_the_share_but_do_in_the_upper_bound

chunk_findings.detail: The phase-scope probe still never calls the metrics service and never passes a phase name. It only gives `_report` an `in_scope` callback over items B then A on tree T, and checks that A is `rerun_same_tree_other_item`. A state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, whole-suite runs only in `beta`, and `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` can still classify the `beta` events, and this test stays green. The tree-history assertion does not lock the dropped `phase` argument.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_reports_only_its_items_but_keeps_the_tree_history

chunk_findings.detail: The short-option narrowing check requires `name[1:].isalpha()`, so an attached `-m` or `-k` value containing digits or underscores is not recognised as narrowing. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest tests -mslow2"`, `_narrows("-mslow2")` returns `False` because `mslow2` is not alphabetic; `_positionals` then returns `["tests"]`, `_ROOT.match("tests")` is true, and `_whole_command` classifies the run as whole-suite. Pytest parses `-mslow2` as `-m slow2`, so the run is marker-narrowed and should not be counted as a whole-suite rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: The new value-option skip list is exact-match and incomplete, so the value of an option that is not listed is still treated as a collected path. Given `command="pytest test_foo.py --doctest-glob tests"`, `_positionals` returns `["test_foo.py", "tests"]` because `--doctest-glob` is not in `_VALUE_OPTIONS`; `_ROOT.match("tests")` is true and `_whole_command` reports a whole-suite run. The `tests` token is the option value (a doctest filename glob), not a collected root path, so this is the same false-positive class the `--basetemp` fix addressed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_positionals

chunk_findings.detail: Attached pytest filters are treated as non-narrowing whenever the expression is not purely alphabetic. `_narrows` only accepts a short cluster when `name[1:].isalpha()`, so `command="pytest tests -ktest_foo"` (and `-ktest1`, `-knot_slow`) does not match `_NARROWING` and is not rejected as narrowing. `_positionals` still sees `tests`, `_ROOT` matches, and `_whole_command` returns True. A keyword-filtered run is counted as a whole-suite run; a second one on the same code tree is classed as an avoidable rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: Value options are an exact allowlist, so any omitted option that takes a following argument still feeds that argument to `_ROOT`. `command="pytest test_foo.py --log-file tests"` (also `--doctest-glob tests`, `--junit-prefix tests`, `--junit-xml tests`) is split into a positional `tests`. That token matches `_ROOT`, so a single-file run is a whole-suite run and a repeat on the same tree is counted as `rerun_same_tree_*` waste. `--basetemp` is skipped; these equally path-or-string-valued options are not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_positionals

chunk_findings.detail: Class `queue_minutes` still publishes a partial sum as the total. The new `whole=True` path is only used for `suite_minutes` and `avoidable_suite_minutes`; `queue_minutes` calls `_minutes(...)` without it. For one class with runs `queue_s=60` and `queue_s=None`, `queue_minutes` is `1.0`, not `None`, and the rendered line has no untimed caveat for queue time (`untimed` only counts missing `suite_s`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` treats any standalone `tests` or `tests/` token in a `unit_tests` command as proof that the whole suite ran, so commands that explicitly exclude the tests directory are misclassified as whole-suite runs. For example, given one real whole-suite run `pytest tests/` on a clean tree and a later `unit_tests` event on the same clean tree with command `pytest --ignore tests/`, `_is_suite` returns `True` for the second event, `classify` puts it in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`, and `build` reports an avoidable share of `1/2`. The second command does not run the whole `tests/` directory, so it should not be in `runs` at all; the correct report for that input has `runs=1`, `avoidable=0`, and `avoidable_share=0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_is_suite

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` returns a partial sum when some per-run values are missing, silently reporting an incomplete class total as if it were the figure. For example, a class containing one run with `elapsed_s=600` and one run with `elapsed_s` absent gets `suite_minutes=10.0` instead of `None` with an `unavailable` explanation. The module contract says a figure the log cannot give is `None` with a reason, but this input produces a non-`None` class minutes figure that cannot be trusted as the total.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: A phase-scoped suitewaste query is classified against the whole log. The handler rejects an unknown phase, then calls `SW.build(events, cfg, now, probes, since=floor)` and never passes `phase`, while `swarm` on the same path does filter. Given events where phase `a` has only unavoidable whole-suite runs and phase `b` has avoidable ones, `metrics` view `suitewaste` with phase `a` still folds `b` into the avoidable share (and the reason breakdown), so the figure is not the phase the caller asked for.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:_own_fold

chunk_findings.detail: `seen` stores only the first item that covered a code tree, so a later rework by another item is not classed as a same-item rerun. Given lane-b then lane-a then lane-a again on tree key K, the third run is `rerun_same_tree_other_item` because `seen[K]` is still lane-b. The module contract says a rerun is same-item when an earlier run of that tree was by the same item, so that input is `rerun_same_tree_same_item`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:131

chunk_findings.detail: Unplaced runs are unknown, but they still sit in the avoidable-share denominator and can refute the falsifier. With minimum 1, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and four `unplaced` rows give `avoidable_share` 0.2 and `falsifier.holds` false (`REFUTED`), even though those four name no tree git can read and the only placed run was avoidable. The claim “under 25 percent avoidable” is not shown; the unknowns are treated as non-avoidable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:191

chunk_findings.detail: The new phase filter excludes out-of-phase events from `SW.build` entirely, so they are also removed from the tree-history evidence used to decide whether an in-phase run is a rerun. Given `state` with `item-a` in phase `p` and `item-b` in phase `q`, and an event log containing (1) a whole-suite run by `item-b` on tree key `K`, then (2) a whole-suite run by `item-a` on the same tree key `K`, `metrics suitewaste --phase p` builds `scope` that returns false for `item-b`; the first run is never seen by the classifier, so the `item-a` run is reported as `first_run` with `avoidable_share` 0. The phase totals should omit the `item-b` run’s count/minutes, but the `item-a` run is still avoidable because an earlier run on the same code tree existed; this change reports it as unavoidable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:129 (`scope` / `_own_fold`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-command detector only rejects exact option names in `_NARROWING`, so a pytest run that ignores the suite through a similarly named option is still treated as whole. For a `unit_tests` event whose command is `pytest --ignore-glob=tests/*.py tests/`, `shlex.split` yields `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py`; `t.split("=")[0]` is `--ignore-glob`, which is not in `_NARROWING`, and the token is skipped as an option. The remaining positional `tests/` matches `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns True and `_is_suite` counts the event as a whole-suite run, even though `--ignore-glob=tests/*.py` explicitly excludes the test files in `tests/`. This inflates whole-suite counts and can change the avoidable share.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper = avoidable / placed` is used to decide the falsifier and is described as an upper bound, but it is not a bound on the total avoidable share once `unplaced` runs exist. With `minimum=1`, one placed non-avoidable run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `avoidable=0`, `placed=1`, `upper=0.0`, and `falsifier.holds` false, so the output treats the “under 25 percent avoidable” condition as met even though those 99 unplaced runs could all be same-item reruns, making the true share 99/100. Conversely, one placed `rerun_same_tree_same_item` run and 99 `unplaced` runs gives `upper=1.0` and `holds` true even though the true share could be 1/100 if the unplaced runs were first runs. Thus unknown trees can still drive the falsifier in either direction, contrary to the comment and the stated all-runs falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:avoidable_share_of_placed

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert not whole("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")` requires `_whole_command` to reject a command that includes the whole suite root `tests/`. Since the same test asserts `whole("pytest ./tests/")`, adding a file path inside that same root cannot make the command anything other than a whole-suite collection: `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/` still collects the entire `tests/` directory. If a `unit_tests` event uses that command as a rerun on a tree already run by the same item, this test locks in classifying the event as not a full-suite run, so the rerun is omitted from `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and the reported avoidable share is undercounted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:192

chunk_findings.detail: `_NARROWING` treats `--ff` as suite-narrowing, but pytest `--ff` / `--failed-first` still runs every test and only reorders failures first. Given a recorded whole-suite command `pytest --ff tests/` (or `pytest tests/ --ff`) after a real `pytest tests/` on the same clean tree, `_whole_command` returns False, the rerun is dropped from `runs`, and `build` under-counts avoidable suite minutes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The parser never consumes option arguments and does not treat `--ignore-glob` as narrowing, so it both misses real whole-suite runs and still accepts narrowed ones. `pytest --junitxml tests/out.xml tests/` (or `pytest --basetemp tests/tmp tests/`) has a non-option token `tests/out.xml` / `tests/tmp` that fails `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns False even though the selected path is the whole `tests/` tree. The inverse, `pytest tests/ --ignore-glob='test_*.py'`, has no token in `_NARROWING` and a root `tests/` path, so it returns True and is classed as a whole-suite rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: `test_unknown_trees_cannot_refute_the_falsifier` locks the falsifier to the wrong verdict on its own fixture. Two placed runs on tree `T` (first plus one same-item rerun) and three unplaced runs give `avoidable_share` 0.2 and `avoidable_share_of_placed` 0.5, and the test requires `falsifier.holds is True`. The prior contract treats `holds` false as the “under 25 percent avoidable” claim being refuted. Unknowns must not force that refutation via the diluted 0.2, but the placed share is 0.5, which is not under 25 percent, so `holds` must be false (or unavailable), not true. An implementation that follows this assertion reports the falsifier as holding when half of the runs git can place were avoidable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:182

chunk_findings.detail: The probe named for the confirmed partial-sum defect never builds a class that mixes a timed run and an untimed run. `_log` of item `A` with `_ev("aaaaaaa1")` and item `B` with only `tree_sha` puts the timed run in `first_on_tree` and the untimed run alone in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`. Asserting `suite_minutes is None` on that one-run class passes even if `_minutes([600, missing])` still returns `10.0`. The input that demonstrates the bug — one class with `elapsed_s=600` and one run with `elapsed_s` absent — is not in the test, so the unfixed summer still goes green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_not_summed_as_zero

chunk_findings.detail: `test_whole_suite_command_detection` does not include the command that confirmed the `_is_suite` misclassification. It rejects `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_slow.py` and `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/`, but not a later `unit_tests` command `pytest --ignore tests/` on a tree already covered by `pytest tests/`. A classifier that only special-cases `--ignore=` (or only an ignore of a subdirectory) still returns true for `--ignore tests/`, so that second event is still counted as a whole-suite rerun and the probe stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_whole_suite_command_detection

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_falsifier` and the renamed `avoidable_share_max` still treat the passed `upper` as a true maximum avoidable share, but the value passed remains the old placed-only ratio rather than a bound over all runs once `unplaced` runs exist. Given a log with 1 placed whole-suite run that is not avoidable and 99 `unplaced` runs, `avoidable=0`, `share=0`, and `upper=0`; `_falsifier(0, 0)` returns `holds=False` and `verdict="refuted"`, and `text` prints `at most 0% if every unplaced run re-ran a tree`. But those 99 unknown-tree runs could all be avoidable reruns, making the maximum true avoidable share 99/100, so the under-25% falsifier cannot be refuted from this data. The upper bound must include the unplaced runs (for example, `(avoidable + unplaced) / runs`) or the falsifier must remain undetermined when unplaced runs exist.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_falsifier

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten probe still never creates a class containing both a timed and an untimed run. The fixture puts A's timed rerun alone in `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and B's untimed rerun alone in `rerun_same_tree_other_item`. Therefore an implementation of `_minutes` that sums only present `elapsed_s` values (`[600, None] -> 10.0`) passes the assertions, even though the class would have `untimed == 1` and incomplete minutes. The previous confirmed partial-sum defect remains untested; a mixed class (for example, A first timed, A second timed, and A third with only `tree_sha` on the same tree) is needed to demonstrate it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: Prefix `startswith` treats non-narrowing pytest options as suite-narrowing. `_NARROWING` contains `--lf`, and `--lfnf=all`.startswith(`--lf`) is true, so `_whole_command("pytest --lfnf=all tests/")` returns False even though `--lfnf` only sets last-failed-no-failures behavior and the selected path is the whole `tests/` tree. A later `unit_tests` event with that command on a tree already covered by `pytest tests/` is dropped from `runs`, so avoidable suite-minutes are under-counted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement `any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` still does not consume option arguments, so a directory that is only an option value counts as the suite root. For `pytest --basetemp tests/ tests/test_a.py`, `shlex` yields args `--basetemp`, `tests/`, `tests/test_a.py`; nothing matches a `_NARROWING` prefix, `_ROOT` matches the `--basetemp` value `tests/`, and `_whole_command` returns True. Pytest collects only `tests/test_a.py`. The same false whole-suite classification hits `pytest --rootdir tests/ tests/unit/test_a.py`. A same-item rerun recorded with that command is then counted as avoidable whole-suite waste.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:93

chunk_findings.detail: `test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes` still never puts a timed run and an untimed run in the same class, so it does not lock the partial-sum bug the probe was supposed to catch. `_log` records item A twice on tree `T` with `_ev` (elapsed present) and item B once on `T` with only `tree_sha`. That yields `rerun_same_tree_same_item` = (1, 10.0, 0) and `rerun_same_tree_other_item` = (1, None, 1). Both assertions pass if `_minutes` drops missing elapsed and returns the sum of the timed samples alone: a same-item class of `elapsed_s=600` plus one run with no elapsed would still report `suite_minutes == 10.0` and `untimed == 1`, and this test would not fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:216

chunk_findings.detail: The new short-option check only inspects the first two characters of an argument, so a combined short option whose last flag is `-k` or `-m` is not treated as narrowing. For the common invocation `pytest -vk tests/` (equivalent to `-v -k tests/`), `_narrows('-vk')` returns False because `arg[:2]` is `-v`; `_positionals` then treats the following `tests/` as a positional path, `_ROOT.match` matches it, and `_whole_command` returns True. The run is keyword-narrowed, not a whole-suite run, so it can be classified as whole and later runs on the same tree can be counted as avoidable reruns. The same failure occurs for combined marker options such as `pytest -vm marker tests/`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: Switching narrowing from a prefix test to an exact option name drops the companion flags the old `--sw` / `--stepwise` prefixes used to reject. Given `pytest --sw-skip tests/` or `pytest --stepwise-skip tests/`, `_narrows` is false for every arg and `_positionals` still sees `tests/`, so `_whole_command` returns True. Pytest still stops at the next failure after skipping the first, the same early exit `--stepwise` is listed to exclude, so that run is counted as a full-suite run and its suite-minutes land in the waste totals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_narrows

chunk_findings.detail: The new whitelist treats `-x` as an ordinary whole-suite flag, and `_VALUE_FLAGS` likewise admits `--maxfail`, but both options can make pytest stop before the whole suite has run. For a log entry with command `pytest -x tests/` that fails on the first test, the command uses only whitelisted flags and the positional `tests/`, so it is classified as a whole-suite run and, if the tree code matches an earlier run, can be counted as avoidable and contribute its partial duration as suite-minutes. This is the same class of early-exit behavior that the confirmed previous finding said should not be counted (`--stepwise-skip`), so counting `-x`/`--maxfail` as full-suite runs misclassifies partial runs as full-suite waste.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_PLAIN_FLAGS

chunk_findings.detail: The new `-n` special case uses `re.fullmatch(r"-n\S+", a)`, so any token that merely begins with `-n` is accepted as the xdist execution flag. Given `pytest -nfoo tests/`, the token `-nfoo` matches that regex and `tests/` matches `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns `True`. Pytest will not run the suite in this case: `-n` requires an integer or `auto`, so `-nfoo` is a usage error, yet the metric would count the command as a whole-suite run and charge its minutes to the suite-waste classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `queue_minutes` to pass `whole=True` makes the queue total unavailable whenever any run in the class has `queue_s is None`, but queue time is only expected for runs that actually queued. For a normal class such as `rerun` containing one queue-integrator run with `queue_s=120` and one direct `ci`/`unit_tests` run with `queue_s=None`, this line returns `None` instead of `2.0`, so the report hides known queue minutes and treats available queue data as unavailable. The missing queue time on non-queued runs should be treated as zero, or `whole=True` should be applied only to runs that are expected to have queue time.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:queue_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion `assert not whole("pytest --ff tests/")` encodes a false negative for a full-suite run. `--ff` is pytest’s failed-first option, not `--lf`/`--last-failed`: it still collects and runs every test under `tests/`, only changing execution order. Given an event-log entry for a `unit_tests` command `pytest --ff tests/` with a recorded duration, the suite-waste report will not count that run as a whole-suite run, omitting its suite/queue minutes and distorting the avoidable-share denominator for a run that is actually full-suite.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:212

chunk_findings.detail: `test_whole_suite_command_detection` now requires `SW._whole_command("pytest --ff tests/")` and `SW._whole_command("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")` to be false. `--ff` / `--failed-first` only reorders; pytest still collects and runs every test under `tests/`. A root positional still collects the whole tree even when another node id is also passed, which the previous assertion documented. Both invocations are full-suite runs, so the new expectations lock the classifier into dropping their suite-minutes from the avoidable share.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:213

chunk_findings.detail: The `suitewaste` branch accepts a `phase` argument (and the caller has already validated that it exists) but then silently drops it: `SW.build` is called only with `events`, `cfg`, `now`, `probes`, and `since=floor`, with no `phase` passed. Given a state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, and whole-suite runs only in `beta`, a call such as `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` returns the whole-suite classification and avoidable share for all events, including those from `beta`, as though they belonged to `alpha`. If `suitewaste` is intentionally global, the view should reject or explicitly ignore the phase parameter at the API/surface boundary; silently accepting and discarding it makes phase-scoped metrics wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:_own_fold

chunk_findings.detail: The whole-suite test detection is based only on a standalone `tests`/`tests/` token, so it both over- and under-classifies `unit_tests` runs. For example, a `unit_tests` event with evidence command `pytest tests -k test_one` (or `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_slow.py`) matches `_WHOLE` because it sees `tests` followed by whitespace, so `_is_suite` returns True and the run is counted/classified as a whole-suite run even though it runs only a subset. Conversely, `pytest ./tests` is a whole-directory run but does not match because `tests` is preceded by `/`, not start/whitespace, so that run is omitted. Either input changes `runs`, class counts, and `avoidable_share`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_WHOLE

chunk_findings.detail: `_minutes` silently sums only the known values, so class and avoidable minute totals can be incomplete but still reported as complete figures. For example, if a class has two runs, one with `elapsed_s=60` and one with missing/invalid `elapsed_s` (so `suite_s=None`), `classes[c]["suite_minutes"]` becomes `1.0`, not `None`, even though the class total suite minutes are unknown and could be much larger. The same applies to `avoidable_suite_minutes` when some avoidable reruns lack `elapsed_s`. This contradicts the module’s contract that a figure the log cannot give is `None` with an unavailable reason, not a partial/zero-looking total.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_suite` returns false unless `evidence.command` is a non-empty string, before the `gate == "ci"` check. A `gate.passed` (or failed) event with `gate=ci`, `tree_sha` `abcdef1+clean`, and `elapsed_s` set but command omitted is dropped by `runs`, so it never receives a class and is missing from `avoidable_share`. The module’s own definition counts every `ci` verdict as a whole-suite run; the command test only belongs on `unit_tests`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:79

chunk_findings.detail: `_WHOLE` only matches a `tests` token bounded by whitespace or the ends of the string, so a real whole-directory `unit_tests` command is not a suite run. Given `command="pytest ./tests/"`, `gate=unit_tests`, a clean sha, and `kind=passed`, `_WHOLE.search` fails (`/` precedes `tests`), `runs` omits the event, and both the class counts and the avoidable share are computed on the wrong set. The same pattern false-positives `pytest tests/test_foo.py --basetemp tests` because the trailing `tests` token matches even though the suite directory was not run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `avoidable_share` is `avoidable / n` where `n` includes `unplaced` runs, which are defined as not avoidable and not classifiable. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, share is 0.1, `falsifier.holds` is false, and `text` prints `REFUTED`, even though the only run git could place was avoidable (share 1.0 if unplaced were left out of the denominator). Unknown trees therefore count as evidence against the cache and can trip the 25% falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:175

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-suite detector still misclassifies ordinary pytest invocations because it scans the entire command line for “narrowing” tokens instead of only pytest arguments. Given `command="python -m pytest tests"`, `shlex.split` produces `['python', '-m', 'pytest', 'tests']`; the `any(...)` check sees `-m` and returns `False`, so `_is_suite` drops a real whole-suite run even though `-m` here is the Python module option, not pytest marker selection. Conversely, `command="pytest tests --ignore-glob=tests/test_slow.py"` is accepted as a whole-suite run because `--ignore-glob` is not in `_NARROWING`, even though that option deliberately excludes a test file from the run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: `build` now filters by `in_scope` before calling `classify`, so out-of-scope runs no longer contribute to the tree history used to decide whether an in-scope run is a rerun. If a passed run for item `beta` on clean tree `abcdef1+clean` is followed by a passed run for item `alpha` on the same tree, calling with `in_scope=lambda item: item == "alpha"` gives the `alpha` row class `first_on_tree` and avoidable share `0`, because the classifier never sees the earlier `beta` run. That is wrong for the stated metric: the `alpha` run is a rerun on a tree whose code paths already ran, so it should be classified as `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and counted as avoidable while still leaving `beta` out of the reported totals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed partial-minute defect still stands: `_minutes` returns `round(sum(known) / 60.0, 2)` whenever at least one value is known. For a class containing one run with `elapsed_s=60` and one run whose `elapsed_s` is missing or invalid, the class `suite_minutes` becomes `1.0`, not `None`, so a partial sum is still reported as if it were the complete class total. The diff adds a docstring saying an `untimed` count is reported beside the minutes, but the changed build path does not add that count to the class totals, so the reported minutes can still be incomplete while appearing complete.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed falsifier denominator defect also remains: `avoidable_share` is still computed over all scoped rows, including `unplaced` rows that are defined as not classifiable. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, the share is `0.1`, `falsifier.holds` is false, and the output reports `REFUTED`, even though every run that git could place was avoidable (share `1.0` if unknown trees were excluded). The new `in_scope` filtering does not change this for the default no-phase call, so unknown trees continue to count as evidence against the cache-first conclusion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The new `upper` value is used as the falsifier’s decisive share and is described as an upper bound, but `avoidable / placed` is not an upper bound on the overall avoidable share. The unplaced runs are unknown and could be avoidable; excluding them from the denominator can make the reported share too low. For example, with `minimum=1`, suppose there are 10 whole-suite runs: 9 are placed, of which 2 are avoidable and 7 are not, and 1 is unplaced. Then `placed=9`, `avoidable=2`, `upper=2/9≈22%`, so `falsifier.holds` is false and `text` reports the cache-first order as refuted. If that one unplaced run is actually a same-tree rerun, the avoidable share is `3/10=30%`, above the 25% threshold, so the data do not establish a refutation. The comment’s premise is false: the correct upper bound accounting for unknown trees would include the unplaced runs in the numerator, not simply drop them from the denominator.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:upper

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `not whole("pytest tests/test_a.py tests/")`, but that command is a whole-suite run: pytest treats `tests/` as a directory argument and collects the entire suite, while the extra `tests/test_a.py` argument only adds a duplicate/redundant selection. If `_whole_command` follows this assertion, a `unit_tests` event with command `pytest tests/test_a.py tests/` will not be counted as a whole-suite run. For example, if that is the second run on the same code tree, it should be classified as an avoidable rerun, but it is omitted from `runs` and `avoidable_share`, understating the avoidable share.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_whole_suite_command_detection

chunk_findings.detail: Option values are treated as test paths. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest tests --basetemp tests/tmp"`, `kind=passed`, and a clean sha, `tests/tmp` matches `^(\./)?tests` but not `_ROOT`, so `_whole_command` returns False and `runs` drops a whole-directory run. The inverse is `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`: the only token matching that prefix is the basetemp directory `tests`, `_ROOT` matches it, and a single-file run is counted as a whole-suite run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: Narrowing flags are only matched as exact tokens in `_NARROWING`. Given `command="pytest tests -ktest_one"` (argparse accepts the attached short option), `-ktest_one` is not in `_NARROWING`, the only collected path is `tests`, and `_is_suite` returns True for a selected subset. `command="pytest tests --ignore-glob=test_slow.py"` has the same result: `--ignore-glob` is never consulted, so an ignored subset is classified and counted as a whole-suite run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The probe that was supposed to lock the dropped `phase` argument never calls the metrics service and never passes a phase name. It only hands `_report` an `in_scope` callback over two items. A state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, whole-suite runs only in `beta`, and `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` can still classify the `beta` events, and this test stays green. The confirmed service-path drop is therefore not answered by the new test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_leaves_other_items_out

chunk_findings.detail: The untimed-minutes probe never puts a timed run and an untimed run in the same class. Item A is a timed first run on tree T; item B is the only member of `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and has no `elapsed_s`. Summing only the known values over an empty set already yields `None`, so the test passes on the unfixed `_minutes`. Given one class with `elapsed_s=60` and a second run whose `elapsed_s` is missing, the old code still reports `suite_minutes` of `1.0` instead of unknown.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_not_summed_as_zero

chunk_findings.detail: `_whole_command` still treats pytest option values as collection paths. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`, `shlex.split` yields args after `pytest` of `["test_foo.py", "--basetemp", "tests"]`; the changed line `return any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` returns `True` because the `--basetemp` value is `tests`, even though pytest collects only `test_foo.py`. If this single-file run occurs twice on the same code tree, the second run is counted as a whole-suite rerun and inflates the avoidable share, while a command such as `pytest tests --basetemp -m` can be incorrectly rejected because an option value starts with `-m`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The new falsifier and output treat `upper` as a true upper bound on the overall avoidable share (`avoidable_share_max`, “at most … if every unplaced run re-ran a tree”), but the value passed in is still the old `avoidable_share_of_placed` value (`avoidable / placed`); this diff renames the key and changes the verdict logic but does not recompute `upper` as the maximum possible share. For example, with 5 placed whole-suite runs of which 1 is avoidable and 1 unplaced run, `upper = 1/5 = 0.20` and `share = 1/6`, so `_falsifier` returns `holds=False` and the text reports “refuted” and “at most 20% …”. If that unplaced run is avoidable, the true overall avoidable share is `2/6 = 33%`, so the report falsely refutes the cache-first order and understates the possible share. This is the previously confirmed upper-bound defect still present in the new `_falsifier`/max-key path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_falsifier / `avoidable_share_max`

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test is still only a direct unit test of an `in_scope` callback; it never passes a phase to the metrics service or exercises the `--phase` path that was previously reported as dropped. It calls `_report(ev, ..., in_scope=lambda i: i == "A")`, so it proves that a supplied item predicate keeps tree history, but it does not prove that a phase name such as `alpha` is converted into that predicate. If the service path for `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` still ignores the phase and classifies all items, a state with whole-suite runs only in phase `beta` would still be reported for `--phase alpha`, and this test would remain green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_reports_only_its_items_but_keeps_the_tree_history

chunk_findings.detail: The updated test still does not place a timed run and an untimed run in the same class. `rerun_same_tree_same_item` contains only a timed run, and `rerun_same_tree_other_item` contains only an untimed run. The previously confirmed partial-minute failure mode is a class with one known `elapsed_s` and one missing/invalid `elapsed_s`; that class is never constructed here. If `_minutes` returns the sum of known elapsed values whenever any value is known, a class with one 600-second run and one untimed run would report `suite_minutes == 10.0` and still count the untimed run, but this test would pass because no class has that mixed timed/untimed membership.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The falsifier verdict function `_falsifier` returns `undetermined` when the lower bound reaches or exceeds the threshold (`lower >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, which yields `holds = True` then `verdict = "stands"`), but if `lower < FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper >= FALSIFIER_SHARE`, `lower` is not `>= FALSIFIER_SHARE` and `upper` is not `< FALSIFIER_SHARE`, so `holds` evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. However, if `lower` is `None` or `upper` is `None`, `holds` also evaluates to `None` and the verdict is `"undetermined"`. Given a dataset where `lower = 0.2` and `upper = 0.3` (`FALSIFIER_SHARE = 0.25`), `lower < 0.25` and `upper >= 0.25`, so `holds` becomes `None` (undetermined). But the research principle R-suite-lock-principles-2026-11-12 defines refutation specifically when *even the upper bound* is under the threshold (`upper < FALSIFIER_SHARE`), meaning an upper bound of 30% cannot be refuted; however, a lower bound below 25% with an upper bound at or above 25% does not mean the cache-first order stands either, yet returning `"undetermined"` conflates missing data (`None`) with an inconclusive bound where the upper bound exceeds the threshold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:236

chunk_findings.detail: The option-value half of the whole-suite detector is still wrong after the rewrite. `return any(_ROOT.match(a) for a in args)` treats every token as a collected path, so a directory that is only an option value still forces a suite match. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest test_foo.py --basetemp tests"`, `kind=passed`, and a clean sha, `tests` matches `_ROOT` and `_whole_command` returns True, so a single-file run is counted as a whole-suite run and can be classed `rerun_same_tree_*` (and added to the avoidable share) when it is the second event on that tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:_whole_command

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed unplaced-share defect is not fixed. `share = avoidable / n` still divides by every scoped row, including `unplaced`. With `min_samples=1`, one `rerun_same_tree_same_item` and nine `unplaced` rows, `avoidable_share` is `0.1`, not `1.0`. Those nine rows are defined as not classifiable; leaving them in the denominator still reports a placed-avoidable share of 100% as 10%, which is the figure `has_figures` and the “avoidable N (X%)” line publish. The new upper bound only changes the falsifier verdict to `undetermined`; it does not take unplaced runs out of the share.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/suitewaste.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed probe still does not put a timed run and an untimed run in the same class, so it passes the unfixed `_minutes`. A is a timed pair on tree T (`rerun_same_tree_same_item`: one timed rerun, `suite_minutes` 10.0, `untimed` 0). B is the only member of `rerun_same_tree_other_item` and has no `elapsed_s`, so `suite_minutes is None` is just the empty known-set case. A class with `elapsed_s=60` plus a second run whose `elapsed_s` is missing still reports `1.0` instead of unknown, and this test stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_untimed_runs_are_counted_beside_the_minutes

chunk_findings.detail: The probe still asserts the denominator bug it is named to forbid. The unchanged setup is one placed avoidable rerun plus unplaced runs (1 of 5 overall, 1 of 2 placed), and the edited test still requires `avoidable_share == 0.2` while only adding `avoidable_share_max == 0.8` and `verdict == "undetermined"`. Unfixed code that divides by every scoped row, including `unplaced`, still returns 0.2 and passes. The share that excludes unknown trees is 0.5, which this test never demands.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_unplaced_runs_do_not_count_in_the_share_but_do_in_the_upper_bound

chunk_findings.detail: The phase-scope probe still never calls the metrics service and never passes a phase name. It only gives `_report` an `in_scope` callback over items B then A on tree T, and checks that A is `rerun_same_tree_other_item`. A state with phases `alpha` and `beta`, whole-suite runs only in `beta`, and `ddflow metrics suitewaste --phase alpha` can still classify the `beta` events, and this test stays green. The tree-history assertion does not lock the dropped `phase` argument.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:test_a_phase_scope_reports_only_its_items_but_keeps_the_tree_history

chunk_findings.detail: The short-option narrowing check requires `name[1:].isalpha()`, so an attached `-m` or `-k` value containing digits or underscores is not recognised as narrowing. Given a `unit_tests` event with `command="pytest tests -mslow2"`, `_narrows("-mslow2")` returns `False` because `mslow2` is not alphabetic; `_positionals` then returns `["tests"]`, `_ROOT.match("tests")` is true, and `_whole_command` classifies the run as whole-suite.
